new_public_evidence.source: Turner, Ly & Grünwald (2024), Generic E-variables for exact sequential k-sample tests that allow for optional stopping
new_public_evidence.result: Directly targets whether two or more sequential data streams come from the same source. The resulting e-variables are exact/nonasymptotic and remain type-I-valid under optional stopping and continuation. This is a materially better literature match for the late-start problem than rejection-based online-FWER recycling.

new_public_evidence.source: Hao, Grünwald, Lardy, Long & Adams (2024), E-values for k-Sample Tests with Exponential Families
new_public_evidence.result: Develops e-variables for k samples under same-distribution null versus different exponential-family members; tractable variants use a larger i.i.d. null or conditioning on sufficient statistics. The paper explicitly analyzes Gaussian location but the accessible primary text does not establish a ready-made full unknown-mean-and-variance Gaussian construction, so that extension remains unverified.

new_public_evidence.source: Grünwald, de Heide & Koolen (2024), Safe testing
new_public_evidence.result: Conditional e-variables can be multiplied into a test supermartingale/e-process and preserve type-I error under optional continuation, providing the correct mathematical target for nonshrinking late-start evidence sharing.

derived_results.claim: The strongest late-start route is to represent repeated same-source-vs-changed-source evidence as one continuing k-sample/test-martingale process, rather than as infinitely many fixed-time p-tests with shrinking alpha.
derived_results.reason: Turner et al. provide exact sequential k-sample e-variables with optional continuation, while safe-testing theory states products of conditional e-variables form a test supermartingale. This directly addresses the structural dilution problem if a valid Gaussian full-distribution conditional e-variable can be instantiated for the retained baseline/post streams.

derived_results.claim: Existing accessible exponential-family k-sample results do not yet justify treating unknown-mean-and-variance Gaussian equality as solved.
derived_results.reason: Hao et al. explicitly give Gaussian-location results and a generic exponential-family framework, but the readily verified text does not supply the exact two-parameter Gaussian mean+variance sequential construction needed here. Turner et al. are generic but computational/power details in their published illustration center on Bernoulli streams.

candidate_new.mechanism: Use one same-source-vs-different-source e-process over a frozen pre-change/reference stream and incoming post stream, so late evidence compounds at a fixed global threshold rather than receiving start-index-specific alpha. Reuse sufficient statistics if a full Gaussian e-variable can be derived. Keep the r77 terminal t/F sentinel as an early high-power companion.
candidate_new.main_blocker: Need an exact/valid full Gaussian unknown-mean-and-variance e-variable under the actual stream/reuse filtration, plus proof that fixing/reusing a finite baseline stream and sequentially extending the post stream satisfies the required sampling protocol. Overlapping rolling candidates cannot be multiplied merely because each marginal test is valid.

frontier: Read the Turner/Hao constructions at theorem/formula level and instantiate the same-source null for a two-parameter Gaussian exponential family or prove that the generic construction is computationally usable from count/mean/SSE sufficient statistics.

Check whether a fixed finite baseline stream plus a growing post stream is covered directly by the k-sample test-martingale sampling protocol; if not, derive a safe unequal/asynchronous sampling version or reserve disjoint reference chunks.
Derive expected log-growth/power for KL>=1 and compare against the r77 fixed-time sentinel and existing SNML future-tail channel under equal global PFA.
Do not multiply overlapping fixed-time t/F sentinels unless conditional-e validity under the exact filtration is proved.
Interval-verify r77 first-start constants and derive formal start-index sentinel tradeoff while the e-process route is being closed.
exact_next_action: Open the primary Turner/Hao formulas for their generic/GRO e-variable and determine whether the null 'both groups are the same N(mu,sigma^2)' with alternative 'different Gaussian parameters' yields a computable e-variable from (n,sum,sum_sq) only. Then prove or refute that sequentially appending to only the post group while keeping a frozen baseline group preserves the test-martingale property. If yes, calculate its KL>=1 growth and combine with r77 sentinel; if no, fall back to the existing future-tail e-process and keep the sentinel finite-prefix only.
